title: Okinawa Road Trip in 5 Days | Churaumi, Onna, Chatan, Naha
subtitle: Pick up and return the car at Naha Airport; stay in Chatan, Onna and Naha, with the Churaumi Aquarium and Gyokusendo Cave
summary: Five days driving Okinawa: one night in Chatan, one in Onna, two in Naha, taking in the Churaumi Aquarium, Gyokusendo Cave and the sea. The notes cover the rental rules for a Taiwan licence with a Japanese translation, driving rules in Japan and Okinawa, getting between the airport and town, and seasonal reminders. Chatan's sunset beach, Manzamō and an izakaya are held as alternates.

The hours of the Route 58 bus-priority lane, and whether a Taiwan-issued international driving permit is valid in Japan; please confirm with the motor vehicles office and the rental company.
Licence and car rental (for Taiwan travellers)

Taiwan travellers who drive in Japan need an original Taiwan licence plus its Japanese translation, and must carry both together; several third-party summaries say international driving permits issued in Taiwan are not valid in Japan, so confirm with the motor vehicles office.

Japanese translation: apply over the counter at any motor vehicles office or station in Taiwan; several third-party summaries put the fee at about NT$100 each, with collection in about 1 hour on the spot; if you are already in Japan, apply through the Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office (about 3 to 7 working days) or JAF.

The July 2026 application form of the Yokohama representative office states that driving on a Taiwan licence with its Japanese translation is limited to within one year of entering Japan. Application form: https://www.roc-taiwan.org/uploads/sites/54/2026/07/臺灣駕照之日文譯本申請表-橫濱20260721.pdf
Get the Japanese translation done before you leave: at the counter the rental company checks the documents one by one, and without the translation you cannot take the car.

Book the car online in advance and choose a depot with a free airport shuttle; in this template you take the shuttle to pick up the car after arriving on day 1 and take the shuttle back to the airport after returning it on day 5, about 15 minutes each way.
When you pick up the car, walk around it together and film it, recording any scratches; whether to add collision damage waiver (insurance) is your own decision, so check it on the booking page.
ETC card and navigation: when you book, confirm whether Japanese and Chinese navigation is included and whether you need to rent an ETC card separately.
Driving rules in Japan and Okinawa
Japan drives on the left, with the driver's seat on the right; after a turn it is easy to end up in the wrong lane, so remind yourself to keep left every time you pull away.
Everyone in the car must wear a seat belt; do not hold a phone while driving; zero tolerance for drunk driving.
There is no turning right on red in Japan; pedestrians have priority when you turn, so stop for them.
Speed limits on ordinary roads are mostly 40 to 60 km/h and on the Okinawa Expressway 80 km/h; follow the roadside signs.
Parking: do not park on yellow kerb lines or where no-parking signs stand; city car parks charge by the hour, and spots reserved for kei cars (yellow plates) are off limits.
On Route 58 in central Naha, bus-priority or bus-only lanes apply at peak hours; check the latest rules before you go.
Rural Okinawa has few street lights at night and is very dark, so drive slowly after dark; on the nights of days 1 and 2, avoid driving mountain roads too late.
Fuel: most stations are self-service, so confirm the fuel type in advance (the rental company will tell you), and fill the tank before returning the car.
Between the airport and town (Naha Airport, OKA)

This template: after immigration, walk toward the airport bus stop and wait at the rental shuttle meeting point for the shuttle to the depot, about 15 minutes; the travelogue's author waited about 40 minutes, so leave extra time.

If you are not picking up a car: the Okinawa Urban Monorail (Yui Rail) from Naha Airport Station to Makishi Station near Kokusai-dōri takes about 12 to 15 minutes, with fares on the official site https://www.yui-rail.co.jp/ ; a taxi to Kokusai-dōri takes about 10 to 15 minutes.
Reservations and tickets

Blue Cave snorkelling: book with a snorkelling operator in advance; meeting time is usually 15 minutes before the boat leaves, and the car park forms long queues in peak season, so arrive at least 45 minutes early.
Yakiniku Ryūkyū no Ushi and the agu pork shabu-shabu place: the travelogue's author booked ahead, so reserve in advance.

Churasun 6: reserve on the official site https://www.churasun6.com/ ; ages 20 and over only, with first-show tickets listed at about ¥6,500 including one drink; the travelogue warns that apart from high-fives and photos, touching the dancers is strictly forbidden, and tips are only given when a dancer offers.
Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium: you can buy e-tickets in advance; details and prices are on the official site https://churaumi.okinawa/ .
Gyokusendo Cave (Okinawa World): about ¥2,000 for adults (official fee page), tickets available on the spot.
CAVE OKINAWA: about ¥1,200 for adults, buy on the spot.
Entry
For visa-free entry, register on Visit Japan Web beforehand; check the official site for the latest process.
Pace of the trip
This is a self-drive template with sights spread from north to south, so driving takes up more of the day than in a typical city itinerary; on day 3 the drive from Onna to Naha is about 75 minutes.
On day 4 the first Churasun 6 show starts at 20:30 and lets out around 21:30, later than the 21:00 on other days.
Season

The template is based on a July summer travelogue: Okinawa is very hot in summer with strong UV, so a long-sleeved swimsuit is advised for snorkelling and outdoor sights go early or late in the day; the itinerary works in other seasons, but sea activities should be adjusted to water temperature and weather.

notes.title: Trip overview: how the 5 days run
paragraphs: In and out of Naha Airport, pick up the car on day 1 and return it on day 5, and drive the whole way yourself. Four nights at three bases: Chatan on night 1, Onna Village on night 2, then the last two nights back around Kokusai-dōri in Naha.
Day 1: take the rental shuttle to your car, drive south to Okinawa World for Gyokusendo Cave, then up to Chatan for {@d1-05} and agu pork shabu-shabu for dinner.

Day 2: snorkel at the Blue Cave at Cape Maeda in the morning, lunch at Blue Entrance Kitchen, the limestone cave at CAVE OKINAWA, then about 55 minutes north to {@d2-05}, and dinner back in Onna Village.
Day 3: lunch at Divers Steak, a seaside café at RYUKYU BEACH CLUB, then about 75 minutes south to Naha for Naminoue Shrine, yakiniku for dinner and a stroll on Kokusai-dōri.
Day 4: shopping at PARCO CITY Urasoe with conveyor-belt sushi, Shintoku ramen for dinner, {@d4-03}, and the Churasun 6 gal-bar show in the evening.
Day 5: {@d5-02} first, Okinawa soba for lunch, Naha ASHIBINAA Outlet, and Blue Seal ice cream before returning the car; then check-in, departure and souvenirs at the airport.
Where to sleep: Chatan (around American Village) on night 1, around Onna Village on night 2, then two nights in a row around Kokusai-dōri in Naha.

Getting around: this is a self-drive route. Travellers from Taiwan need the original Taiwanese licence plus a Japanese translation, arranged before departure, since you cannot pick up the car without it. Book the rental ahead and choose a depot with a free airport shuttle, about 15 minutes. Traffic keeps left, rural Okinawa is very dark at night, so drive slowly, and fill the tank before you return the car. The sights are spread from south to north, so driving takes a bigger share than on a city trip; day 3 from Onna to Naha is about 75 minutes. Check the latest rules and timetables before you go.

Who it suits: anyone who wants to drive in Okinawa and take in beaches, a limestone cave, the aquarium and Naha in one trip. Someone has to be comfortable at the wheel; summer is very hot, so put outdoor sights early or late, and wear a long-sleeve swimsuit for snorkelling.
